cusum.note: Around zero: S = max(0, S + sum over the day of (-z - k) / (1 + (n - 1) rho)), z = clvRet / sd; k .25, h 10 as registered Oct 21 (the log likelihood ratio of losing half an sd a bet against the close, at 148:1). Per bet and undeflated, as first run, it stopped a rule earning exactly its stakes' edge 9-52% of the time on the history's own slates; by day and deflated 0-3%. Against the stakes' edge (hL): S = max(0, S - day LLR), the drift test's game-day log likelihood ratio (reference mu1 / 2), stop at hL = ln 99. ln 19 and ln 39 stopped an NFL spread rule at its edge 39% and 21% of the time over 300 bets; ln 99 9%, every other market rule 0-1%. The window test (last 300, clustered t < -1) is no longer a stop: checked at every build from 50 bets, with a clustered se that few game days put under the iid one, it and the per-bet CUSUM stopped a rule at its stakes' edge 15-54% of the time.

drift.note: Overfit test for every pick rule from its clock (so every new or refit rule): Wald's SPRT, H1 the rule is worth its held-out backtest's clvRet with its edge over a fair coin x units.TIMING x units.LEAK (the edge its stakes assume), H0 it is worth 0. Game-day LLR deflated by the within-slate correlation of close value on the rule's held-out picks (clvIcc; units' rho is the correlation of results, about 0, and made the LLR up to 2.5x too large). Pause at LLR <= -ln B (a stop, cleared only by a refit), confirm at >= ln A (test retires; the close switch keeps running). A 19 / B 19 as registered Nov 1; the error rates per rule are in `rates`.
